answer: Divergent-Response Identity Challenge. Each identity must answer a fresh random challenge derived from its own history; honest agents answer independently and land on separate points, like trees in an orchard. Clones share state, so they must return identical answers, collapsing to one point on a reef of verification. An agent whose responses match too closely is flagged, and every matching copy pays the same per-identity challenge cost. Sybils therefore multiply cost without multiplying distinct answers, making each fake identity a paid knoll of redundant effort.
